Checked Proof 1.1–3.1 and the exact Euclidean cohomology convention, global bundle complex, harmonic regularity, finite kernel and Hodge suppliers. Degree-zero incoming and degree-one outgoing spaces vanish, so the displayed groups have the correct kernel/quotient typing. The degree-one projection kills exactly the exact forms, is onto the smooth harmonic kernel, and inclusion followed by quotient is its inverse. Both groups are finite dimensional; their zero cases are included because a zero harmonic space forces a zero quotient. The fixed Dolbeault complex uses only holomorphic structure, so metric changes alter harmonic representatives while leaving these vector spaces and dimensions fixed. Full AC is inherited without new choice. Demailly V printed268 and VI (7.2) printed309 agree; McMullen printed119 states a sheaf-cohomology comparison, not a substitute for this proof. Pre/post item hashes agree and the only change is the zero-case contract row, which now refers to this actual projection argument rather than another item duality proof.

Checked Verification 1.1–2.1 and the actual quotient-action and Hodge/operator supplier statements. Disks of radius <1/2 have disjoint translates. The quotient is open; finite lattice intersection with bounded disks supplies positive separation of inequivalent points, hence Hausdorffness. Images of a countable plane base give second countability; continuous image gives connectedness and nonemptiness; the closed unit square supplies compactness. Translation transitions form a holomorphic atlas and descend the flat metric, trivial bundle and dbar z. The explicit derivative is pi cos(2pi x), nonzero at zero. For any smooth exact harmonic a=D b, the actual Hilbert adjoint identity gives ||a||²=<b,D* a>=0, so the nonzero example is not harmonic. Positive metric weights and declared AC hold. Demailly VI (4.5) printed297 confirms compact complex tori as context. Pre/post item and contract changed while Example and manifest are preserved. Checked both verification steps and the exact topological extreme-value supplier clause2 and local maximum-modulus theorem. A harmonic maximal-domain function has a smooth holomorphic representative. The modulus attains a maximum on nonempty compact X using the newly cited topological theorem, without a metric/topology bridge. Its maximum-value level set is closed, and every point in it has a connected chart disk where maximum modulus makes the value constant; it is therefore open and equals connected X. Conversely a constant lies in the maximal domain with zero derivative in the adjoint domain, hence in the block Laplacian domain. Nonemptiness and positive volume make 1 a nonzero L2 class, so the kernel is exactly one dimensional, for any supplied positive weight and compatible metric. The actual source/dependency/contract replacement is mathematically appropriate. Pre/post item and contract changed, with Example and manifest preserved.
